plain_english_policy: This bill updates Alabama state law to allow farmers to legally sell yellow perch that they raise in their own farm ponds without needing a special permit from the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, provided other conditions are met. Currently, selling game fish caught or taken from freshwater is generally prohibited unless specific exemptions apply (like hatchery stock). This bill explicitly adds 'yellow perch' to the list of nonnative game fish raised for human consumption that can be sold in farm ponds under existing permit rules.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would expand the legal ability for Alabama farmers and pond managers to commercially sell yellow perch harvested from their private or public freshwater farm ponds. It aligns with a policy direction of supporting aquaculture and local food production by reducing regulatory barriers for specific species while maintaining oversight through existing permitting requirements.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives McLaughlin and McDaniel advanced this bill to amend the Code of Alabama 1975 regarding game fish sales.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would add yellow perch raised in farm ponds to the list of game fish exempt from the prohibition on sale under the same conditions."

"nor shall it apply to the sale of nonnative game fish raised for human consumption... nor shall it apply to the sale of yellow perch, largemouth bass, shellcracker, and bluegill bream raised in farm ponds; provided, that, prior to any sale provided for in this section, the seller shall have first obtained a permit for the sale from the Commissioner, Department of Conservation and Natural Resources."
